description: TESP is a platform for designing and testing transactive energy systems, in which market signals coordinate many distributed devices and buildings. It is developed by Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, with copyright held by Battelle Memorial Institute from 2017 to 2025, so that researchers can build and evaluate transactive control agents without assembling a large simulation stack themselves. TESP uses the HELICS co-simulation framework to coordinate GridLAB-D for distribution grids and houses, EnergyPlus for large buildings, AMES/PSST and PYPOWER for transmission and markets, and ns-3 for communications, and adds transactive agents, growth models for multi-year system change, and evaluation scripts. Test cases include the NIST TE Challenge 2, the SGIP use case 1 and an 8-bus ERCOT system, with double-auction real-time and day-ahead markets and a consensus mechanism for large buildings. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub under a BSD-style licence at no cost, runs natively on Linux, and is actively maintained (latest commit September 2026, 39 tags). Caveats: installation bundles several third-party simulators, and the focus is market-based control, not hazards. Simulation uses are agent-based studies of markets, demand flexibility and grid operation. Related records: platform-helics is its coupling layer.
